title: Hip-to-ankle sequencing
effort: Connect rapid hip extension through the ankle without compensatory trunk or arm motion.
quality_marker: In E1 record whether the six listed releases show hip drive preceding a smooth forefoot finish, with no second dip or arm curl. Keep ball, start position and trajectory noted; do not compare distance with the earlier different scoop executions. Use the listed attempts only; a miss or invalid attempt consumes the dose. Record actual attempts, setup and any substitutions; no bonus tests or comparison across unlike tasks.
brief: The held-hinge leg-driven release leads, with small forward ankle impulses, familiar hip reversals, a stance-leg finish, flexed-knee ankle output and a seated knee/hip start supporting distinct parts of the chain. Landing exposure falls and primary work returns to bilateral bases.

explosive.name: Medicine Ball Scoop Toss — held hinge to forefoot finish
explosive.key: Medicine Ball Scoop Toss — held hinge to forefoot finish
explosive.job: Main hip-to-ankle sequence transferring leg force into an upward-forward release.
explosive.cue: Hold a comfortable hinge for 2 s with long arms and a light ball. Drive hips forward and rise onto forefeet as the ball floats upward-forward; keep forefeet grounded and do not add an arm curl, second dip or lumbar arch. Let the ball land, never catch.
explosive.replacement: a light-dumbbell held-hinge to rapid tall rise with feet flat, six total reps in the same 2 × 3 structure and 90 s set recovery; log no throws and no ankle finish if omitted
explosive.identity: medicine-ball-scoop-toss family; held hinge with explicit grounded ankle finish proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: The held hip start and deliberate ankle finish differ from Week 5 knee-led continuous dip. It links contributors without adding a landing or an overhead pressing task.
explosive.rest_text: 90 s between complete set rounds; 20 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Ankle Pogo — three small forward advances
explosive.key: Ankle Pogo — three small forward advances
explosive.job: Direct a small ankle-led impulse forward while maintaining a tall aligned body.
explosive.cue: Three low consecutive bilateral pogos advancing only a little each time; knees remain soft, not locked. Keep the whole series inside the marked short area and absorb/stop the third landing.
explosive.replacement: three isolated supported rapid bilateral calf rises without flight or travel, with 10 s between reps and the same 90 s transition, if rhythm, ankle comfort or reception fails; log zero landings and the extra actual reset time
explosive.novelty_reason: Changes the impulse direction from Week 2 in-place elastic work. Only three low contacts are used; high bounds would duplicate the broader jump curricula.

explosive.name: Kettlebell Swing — continuous two-hand chest-height float
explosive.key: Kettlebell Swing — continuous two-hand chest-height float
explosive.job: Reapply hip force after the retained implement returns, with no ground landing.
explosive.cue: Use a light bell and established hinge; three continuous hip-driven swings to chest-level float. Guide the return, keep ribs stacked and park after the third. No arm lift or squat bounce.
explosive.replacement: three separated parked swings with full 10 s resets if continuous timing is unconfirmed; add actual time
explosive.identity: kettlebell-swing; migration 472 continuous two-hand source variant
explosive.novelty_reason: Three continuous bilateral swings retain a familiar lengthened-hip reversal to support the new held-hinge release. One-hand or alternating swings would add grip/rotation complexity without a leg-sequencing benefit.

explosive.name: Reverse Lunge to Knee Drive — fast grounded return
explosive.key: Reverse Lunge to Knee Drive — fast grounded return
explosive.job: Drive the stance hip/knee to tall support as the other leg becomes free.
explosive.cue: Bodyweight: step back under control, then drive through the front whole foot and bring the returning thigh forward to a comfortable knee lift; hold 1 s. Front foot stays grounded. Two per stance leg.
explosive.replacement: a quick reverse-lunge return with both feet finishing on the floor at the same per-leg dose if single-support finish fails
explosive.identity: dumbbell-reverse-lunge family; rapid bodyweight knee-drive finish proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Finishes on one stance leg instead of Week 4 two-foot return. This is a continuous return task, not a lunge plus a separate balance drill.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 45 s, then the other leg; 4 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Seated Bent-Knee Calf Raise — fast light rise
explosive.key: Seated Bent-Knee Calf Raise — fast light rise
explosive.job: Express rapid plantar-flexion force with the knee held flexed.
explosive.cue: Sit securely, feet on floor, very light controlled thigh loads if needed; lift heels quickly, hold 1 s and lower 2 s. Keep knee angle fixed; no bouncing or hand pull on the loads.
explosive.replacement: a supported standing bent-knee rapid heel rise at the same bilateral dose if the seated setup fails
explosive.identity: seated-dumbbell-calf-raise parent; rapid light delivery proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Three familiar seated rapid heel rises retain knee-flexed ankle output alongside E2 near-straight-knee elastic impulse. A new single-leg ankle task would add side bouts after Week 7 without a sequencing need.
explosive.rest_text: 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Sit-to-Stand — rapid full-foot push, no flight
explosive.key: Sit-to-Stand — rapid full-foot push, no flight
explosive.job: Integrate knee and hip extension from an externally supported still start.
explosive.cue: Sit briefly on an inspected bench that permits full feet on the floor and a comfortable knee angle. Pause 2 s without rocking, stand quickly using the legs, then sit down under control for 3 s. Feet stay flat; do not push with the arms.
explosive.replacement: three fast grounded squat rises from a 2 s held comfortable squat if the bench does not fit, with the same reset and no flight
explosive.identity: Proposed rapid still-start sit-to-stand execution; not the seated-jump task
explosive.novelty_reason: Uses a seated still start and grounded whole-foot finish, unlike the earlier flight task. It provides knee/hip force with no additional receiving demand.
explosive.rest_text: 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

resilience.name: Tibialis Raise — wall-supported
resilience.job: Light ankle dorsiflexor loading to control foot position before a stable push/landing.
resilience.cue: Back against an inspected wall, heels on floor; lift forefeet 2 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Adjust foot distance to stay easy.
resilience.replacement: a seated unweighted toe raise through comfortable range
resilience.identity: Verified family: tibialis-raise; wall-supported execution declared

resilience.name: Seated Band Ankle Eversion — light
resilience.job: Light outer-ankle strengthening to resist rolling over the foot edge during the push.
resilience.cue: Heel supported; hand-held light band draws the forefoot inward. Move forefoot outward 2 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s while the knee stays still.
resilience.replacement: gentle hand resistance through a smaller range at the same per-leg dose
resilience.identity: Proposed exact dynamic execution; ankle-eversion family referenced, no exact ID
resilience.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 30 s, then the other leg; 10 total reps; 60 s before the next exercise/section

primary.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
primary.job: Hip extension from a lengthened hinge, with the trunk transmitting rather than supplying the motion.
primary.cue: Lower 3 s with soft knees, bells close and hips back; stand in about 1 s. Stop range before back rounding or pelvic tuck.
primary.replacement: a lighter two-dumbbell hinge through a shorter controlled range
primary.identity: Verified local family: dumbbell-romanian-deadlift; supported/load/range details are declared coaching executions
primary.rest_text: 120 s between complete set rounds; 120 s before the next lift preparation

primary.cue: Lower 3 s, stand decisively in about 1 s; hold a manageable goblet load and retain comfortable depth without heels lifting.
primary.replacement: a lighter goblet squat through controlled comfortable range; a two-dumbbell front hold may replace a limiting goblet grip

primary.cue: Use stable hand support if needed; rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s to the floor. Keep knees softly straight and heels tracking over the forefoot.

primary.name: Hamstring Walkout — complete out-and-back cycle
primary.job: Knee-flexor leverage while the pelvis stays raised, distinct from moving through a hip hinge.
primary.cue: Start in a bilateral bridge. Each cycle is two small heel steps out per foot, then two back per foot: eight placements in about 8 s. Keep a soft knee and level hips; never chase a fully straight leg.
primary.replacement: a shorter-lever walkout at the same complete-cycle count; reduce range for sagging or cramp and stop if control does not return

E: Use light resistance or bodyweight that permits visibly rapid force with control. Begin with E1 while fresh. Each row has a distinct job; supporting work stays small. Rest may be extended to 2–3 minutes when speed, control or attention has not returned. Stop for pain, loss of alignment, stiff/asymmetric landing or clear slowing; rest and regress remaining work only if control returns, otherwise record stopped work. Never make up failed attempts. No drop landings or rotational throws are prescribed.
S: Light controlled strengthening, at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Do not chase burn, shaking or pre-fatigue. Reduce load/range when control fades; stop for symptoms.
P: Working sets are challenging at about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Select load/lever from demonstrated ability, not age or calendar week. Keep the stated controlled lowering and complete range; no forced repetitions, maximum testing or conditioning circuit. Check late-set and late-session quality; record reductions instead of forcing nominal completion.

setup: Verify ball flight, ceiling, bounce and roll containment before using the main release. Keep the short pogo series well inside the first 3 m with remaining space clear. Bench height must fit the athlete for both sit-to-stand and seated calf work; no adjustable bench is presumed. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.
delivery: Estimate 52–58 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 for an athlete with equipment access. Includes work, resets, listed recovery, preparation, transitions and 10–16 minutes of extra instruction/setup; additional queues, rest or load-finding add time. Existing preparation duration and total booking fit remain unresolved. Never compress needed recovery to fit a clock. One coached focus class per week for twelve weeks. Review actual sport, leg lifting, running, jumping and tumbling before delivery. Initially allow roughly 48–72 hours before another demanding leg exposure when the full schedule permits, adjusting to actual recovery; a week elapsed is not proof of readiness. Resume missed classes without doubling up. No additional full workouts or body-control blocks are prescribed.
progression: Week 7 prescribed eight unilateral takeoffs and eight bilateral landings. Here only three small bilateral pogo landings remain, alongside six separate throws. RDL returns to two rounds at 2 × 5 rather than the older 2 × 6; Goblet Squat 1 × 5 replaces Split Squat, and bilateral straight-knee calf 1 × 6 replaces the single-leg calf. Seven primary rounds/seven bouts contain 32 conventional reps plus two cycles. The second RDL round is a conditional restoration of hinge practice, not permission for heavier loads; hold one round if actual readiness does not support it and log the modification.
audit_findings: The main toss is leg driven with forefeet grounded; throws are not counted as jumps. The three moving pogo receptions are low-amplitude contacts and need their own receiving-quality judgment. Two exact supporting repeats reduce instruction while four related executions solve new start, trajectory or finishing constraints. Independent calf/lead-leg demands decrease instead of rising alongside the release task.
